evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. One file, grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp, contains literal quote and semicolon characters inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols that name C grammar terminals (e.g. a rune for the C `;` token), but these are still bare rule-name symbols with zero declaration forms, not strings or comments.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 158 files individually scanned end to end via a batched while-read loop with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0 in every file, and grep -c for '"' and ';' returning 0 in 157 of them.

books/kestrel/c/syntax/.sys/grammar-operations@useless-runes.lsp: manually inspected; its 179 quote and 1 semicolon occurrences are all inside pipe-escaped rule-name symbols such as (C$::|C17-CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|) and (C$::|C17-CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) naming C grammar terminals, and its head/tail match the same bare-symbol/fire-count-tuple format as the rest of the file and this unit's other .sys files.

books/kestrel/c/syntax/.sys/abstract-syntax-trees@useless-runes.lsp (2253885 bytes, largest) and books/kestrel/c/syntax/tests/.sys/types-to-tynames@useless-runes.lsp (47 bytes, smallest): individually checked, same result.

In books/kestrel/java/language/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp the quote and semicolon characters found by a naive grep belong to pipe-escaped symbol names for Java lexical-grammar terminals (e.g. |CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|), not to string literals or comments; a check for true comment lines (^;) returns 0, confirming the same bare-symbol/tuple format.
